title: Dissociative Identity Disorder - BSV and Vocal Switches
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: BSV / Vocal

BSV / VOCAL SIGNALS: Sudden shifts in voice quality, pitch, accent, or speech style during identity switches. One state may show high arousal + low valence (angry child), another low arousal + flat affect (protector). Amnesia gaps reported. Voice may change mid-sentence with altered prosody, vocabulary, or even handedness in writing samples.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "I don't remember writing that", "Sometimes my voice sounds completely different", "There are others inside who take over".

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: Consistent voice and identity across sessions, no amnesia for daily events, symptoms fully explained by substance or medical condition.

PROVENANCE: Clinical case literature on DID presentation.
